dedupe_keys.name: event correlated outage dataset in america eagle i county outages matched to doe 417 disturbance events 2014 2023

description: The Event-correlated Outage Dataset in America is a processed data set from Pacific Northwest National Laboratory that links power outages to the disturbances that caused them. It combines three public sources: EAGLE-I county outage counts at 15-minute intervals for 2014 to 2023, covering more than 146 million customers; the Electric Emergency Incident and Disturbance Report (DOE-417); and Census county population estimates for 2024 (CO-EST2024-POP). Outages are filtered and aggregated, then matched to each DOE-417 event by location and start and end times, and metrics are defined to quantify the outages tied to each major disturbance. The OEDI submission, also listed on Data.gov, offers Outage Dataset v1 and v2 zip archives with aggregated, merged and event-correlated data, data guidelines for each version and a disclaimer; Data.gov shows the data set last updated on 27 July 2026. Work was funded by PNNL Laboratory Directed Research and Development under the RD2C initiative. Coverage is the United States by county. The zip files are free to download under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: event matching depends on DOE-417 timing and location fields, and EAGLE-I coverage grows over the period. Simulation uses are event-level outage impact and restoration curves for extreme weather and physical attacks. Related records: data-eagle-i-recorded-electricity-outages-us-counties and data-doe-oe-417-electric-disturbance-events are its inputs.
